correctness.rationale: Exact matrix exponential identity yields the Floquet trace and determinant; d>max(a,a^{-1}) implies sigma>0 and both frozen/average unstable. Jury gives exact stability. Exponential smallness localizes stable t near regularly spaced simple zeros of the growing oscillatory coefficient; monotonicity near each zero proves unique component and scaled boundary convergence. Geometric summation gives the total tail coefficient. Standalone checks reproduce matrix exponentials and nine numerical window widths, but infinity follows solely analytically.

value.rationale: The existence of arbitrarily slow fixed-parameter stabilization despite unstable frozen and averaged systems is qualitatively distinct from representative intermediate-time windows. Its sharp exponentially small allowed dwell tolerance and exact finite tail measure quantify an operationally important fragility and explain why coarse numerical stability scans miss the exceptional slow schedules. These global asymptotic invariants were not given by the motivating pointwise criterion.
